answer: To open an earning key, an operator books one surveyed mesa quarry face and splits a uniquely bedded shale flake along a live cleavage that only that morning's strata can produce. The still-damp flake is carried to a numbered municipal wharf scale, where an unannounced inspector steel-stamps the wet-mass and pin-photo into the harbor ledger. Clones collide because one cleavage yields one flake and one berth stamp cannot be taken in two weigh-ins at once; an attacker must book a new mesa face, split a fresh shale flake, and keep a separate live wharf appointment for every extra key.
